title: ::: K-IG 교육 영어듣기훈련프로그램 | 기초2 | 제 001 회 강의 :::
label: [ K-IG 교육 Reading 203 ]

blocks.text: Words like 'English' and 'Korean' have two different meanings. We can say that if a person is English, he speaks English. If he is Korean, he speaks Korean. And so forth. But we cannot always do this because there are exceptions. For example, if a person is Mexican, he speaks Spanish; if he is Belgian, he speaks Dutch, French, or German; if he is Brazilian, he speaks Portuguese. More importantly, we cannot switch the argument and say, "If he speaks German, he is German." He may quite well be Swiss. This is particularly true of the English language.
